Join the People Helping PeopleVelera is the nation’s premier payments credit union service organization (CUSO) and an integrated fintech solutions provider. The company serves more than 4,000 financial institutions throughout North America, operating with velocity to help our clients keep pace with the rapid momentum of change and fuel growth in the new era of financial services. Our purpose: We accelerate partners’ success through innovative financial technology solutions and inspired service.The OpportunityThe Senior IT Security Compliance Analyst provides support for technology compliance programs, including leading and executing functions and duties that may include: consulting and collaborating with business and technology stakeholders at all levels on control design and remediation to migitigate technology risks; participating on large-scale projects; maintaining IT control library/testing general computer and application controls; coordinating and supporting technology components of onsite and virtual audits/assessments, NCUA examinations and client due diligence reviews; performing segregation of duties reviews and user attestations; documenting process flows and compliance-related deliverables; assisting with creation and maintenance of IT and information security policies and standards required to maintain company certifications (e.g., PCI DSS, SOC 1& 2 Type II NIST CSF); coaching and cross-training technology compliance staff. The individual will execute assigned duties to meet stated priorities and SLAs. The individual plays a critical role in driving technology control and compliance practices and adoption across the company. This role directs and advises technical SMEs in the design, implementation, monitoring and reporting of technology control and compliance processes and documentation on premise and in the Cloud.Day In The Life

- With minimal oversight, execute technology compliance and governance duties as assigned to meet company information security & technology compliance standards, industry requirements, and applicable laws and regulations (e.g., PCI DSS, SOC 1& 2 Type II, NIST CSF, NIST AI Risk Mgt).
- Participate on strategic business and client commercialization projects (e.g., consulting, documenting, validating, and testing Blueprint controls); Review, test, and validate user account and security configurations for compliance with information security and technology policies/standards; Collect and maintain appropriate evidence and supporting documentation.
- Collaborate with and advise technical and business unit resources at all levels on designing, implementing, and remediating technology controls that achieve risk and control objectives and meet compliance requirements while striking a balance between costs vs. benefits.
- Execute segregation of duties (SOD) reviews and user attestations of internal/business partner systems and client online banking platforms.
- Document, maintain, and facilitate technology compliance deliverables (e.g., PCI, SOC, Scope Validation, Targeted Risk Assessments, Compensating Control Worksheets, Shared Responsibility Matrices, process flows, department procedures).
- Identify and report on technology control status and metrics; Assist with Audit Committee and Board reporting.
- Coordinate and support technology components of internal/external audits and assessments (e.g., SOC1/2, PCI DSS, NIST CSF, NIST AI Risk Mgt, NACHA) and onsite/virtual client reviews; Drive for timely submission of critical audit and compliance deliverables to ensure successful SOC1, SOC2, PCI and other external audits.
- Perform QA reviews of technology compliance work products (e.g., user attestation packages) and client assistance documentation prior to delivering to internal and external auditors, clients, and business partners.
- Cross-train, coach, and mentor technology compliance team members in performing job functions.
- Support vendor risk governance program, RFPs, and client due diligence responses (e.g., SIG questionnaires, cybersecurity risk assessments).
- Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree in computer science, information systems, cybersecurity, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience required.
- Cybersecurity risk management, governance, and control professional certification required (e.g., CISA, CRISC, CGEIT).
- Other relevant professional certifications preferred (e.g., PCI Internal Security Assessor (ISA), PCI Qualified Security Assessor (QSA), Certificate of Cloud Security Knowledge (CCSK), Project Management Professional (PMP), Certified ScrumMaster (CSM)).
- Eight (8) years of relevant work experience in public accounting firm, IT controls consulting/testing, leading and overseeing SOC 1, SOC 2, PCI/NIST CSF assessments, IT internal/external auditing, and technology risk management required.
- Experience in identification, validation, design, and testing operating effectiveness of general computer and application controls.
- Experience assessing cloud security and controls required.
- Experience in IT Controls Consulting in Fintech, SaaS, or Financial Services required.
- Demonstrated experience serving as primary lead for enterprise PCI-DSS and/or SOC audits including planning, evidence management, auditor coordination, issue remediation, executive reporting, and successful audit completion.
- Theoretical knowledge and practical application of major risk and IT control frameworks, IT industry standards, and financial services regulations surrounding IT (e.g., PCI, NIST CSF, NIST AI Risk Management, FFIEC, NACHA, CMM, COBIT, ITIL, COSO)
- Solid knowledge of independent audit and assessment reports per job function (e.g., SOC1/2, PCI DSS AOC/ROC
- Ability to work with cross-functional technology and business teams
- Ability to apply understanding of IT security/controls risk vs. business impact in decision making
- Ability to influence without authority
- Ability to be flexible and work under high pressure in a complex environment with frequently shifting priorities
- Strong organizational and time management skills; Ability to multi-task and juggle competing tasks under strict deadlines
- Self-starter with minimal management supervision; Ability to take ownership, seeing tasks and projects through to satisfaction and completion
- Interpersonal skills necessary to interact with executive management and to obtain cooperation from all levels of management and other company personnel
- Solid understanding and ability to apply security concepts across a broad scope of information technology areas including cloud, data communications, network design, operations, database structures, operating systems, application development, security risk assessment, and disaster recovery
- Solid knowledge of and experience with various operating system and database platforms (e.g. Windows AD, Azure, Unix, Oracle, SQL)
- Project management skills including ability to manage multiple projects and work effectively with technology and business resources to drive internal control, process improvement, and remediation efforts
- Strong business acumen; ability to communicate compliance and technical requirements into relevant and understandable terms for business personnel and vice versa for technology personnel
- Ability to communicate effectively, both verbally and in written formats
- Demonstrated strong analytical, problem solving, and critical thinking skills
- Ability to work well in team environment
- Ability to exercise discretion, situational awareness, and good judgment in making decisions
- Proficiency in Word, flow charting (e.g., Visio) and advanced features of spreadsheets (Excel)
- Ability to travel as needed to successfully perform position responsibilities, less than 25%
- Ability to maintain confidentiality of materials handled

In 2025, China continued to strengthen its data security and privacy framework, and with the main rules largely in place, regulators have become more active in enforcement. Multinationals operating in China should therefore be prepared for closer scrutiny, particularly in relation to large-scale personal data leaks—especially where the affected data is transmitted or accessible overseas—and should proactively remediate common security gaps (including those involving legacy or unused devices) and maintain a practical incident response plan covering mitigation and, where required, notifications to affected individuals and regulators. Companies should also handle “Important Data” with particular caution, especially in transactions involving government agencies or state-owned enterprises, by embedding appropriate contractual safeguards in data processing and commercial agreements and by monitoring Important Data catalogues and guidance issued by local governments and industry regulators. In addition, cross-border data transfers should be reviewed on an ongoing basis to confirm whether a CAC security assessment, standard contract filing, or other compliance mechanism is required; even where formal filings are not required, companies should conduct data classification and an internal risk assessment covering the data involved, the business rationale, the key risks, and the security measures in place. For further details, please refer to our 2025 annual report on China's data security regime.

Role Overview:

One of our clients, a global leader in the technology industry, requires a Data Protection Officer (PII Compliance) to oversee the implementation and management of PII compliance protocols, ensuring the protection and lawful processing of personal data. This is a contract role that involves working in a dynamic, remote environment to safeguard sensitive information. As a Data Protection Officer, you will play a pivotal role in maintaining adherence to global regulations and balancing data utility and re-identification risks.

Key Responsibilities:

• Oversee the implementation and management of PII compliance protocols, ensuring the protection and lawful processing of personal data.

• Evaluate data flows and documentation to identify, classify, and mitigate risks associated with structural identifiability, including non-obvious PII and proprietary information.

• Develop and maintain data protection policies and procedures to ensure compliance with global regulations, such as GDPR.

• Conduct regular audits and risk assessments to ensure the integrity and security of personal data.

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to implement data protection best practices and provide training on PII compliance.

Required Skills & Qualifications:

• Proven experience in PII compliance and data protection, with a strong understanding of global regulations, such as GDPR.

• Expertise in data management, data privacy, and compliance, with the ability to evaluate data flows and identify risks.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to develop and implement effective data protection policies and procedures.

• Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work with cross-functional teams and provide training on PII compliance.

• Strong attention to detail and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects and priorities.

More About the Opportunity:

This role offers the opportunity to work with a global leader in the technology industry, contributing to the development of innovative AI models and solutions. As a Data Protection Officer, you will play a critical role in ensuring the protection and lawful processing of personal data, and will have the opportunity to work with a talented team of professionals who are passionate about data protection and compliance.

Equal Opportunity Employer:

We hire based on skills and expertise. All qualified candidates are welcome regardless of background, experience, or prior employment history. Applications are reviewed solely on demonstrated technical ability and qualifications.

# Risk Advisory GRC Consultat - Remote (USA)

#### Echelon Risk + Cyber Washington, DC 1 month ago Be among the first 25 applicants See who Echelon Risk + Cyber has hired for this role No longer accepting applications

- Report this job

About us: At Echelon Risk + Cyber, we believe in defending the basic human right to security and privacy. We are looking for an exceptional Risk Advisory GRC Consultant to support the execution of Risk Advisory client engagements. This includes leading and executing relevant tasks, as well as assisting in developing service deliverables and internal processes that will drive value for the team and clients.Our next team member will be authentic, articulate, and passionate about Cybersecurity, and will be unafraid to roll up their sleeves and dive deep into the unknowns, using their security expertise to identify opportunities to increase Echelon Risk + Cyber's overall capabilities internally and for our clients.At Echelon, you will have the opportunity to engage with systems at the cutting edge of technology. We allow our employees to build from the ground up and make an impact across the organization. We look for driven, proactive people eager to contribute to a distinct and thriving Cybersecurity services organization that can adapt to a rapidly changing environment.This is a remote position from anywhere in the USA.What You Will Do

- Perform SOC 2 Type I/II readiness assessments and support attestation engagements, including scoping, control evaluation, gap identification, and remediation guidance
- Conduct ISO 27001 gap assessments, internal audits, and certification support engagements for clients across a range of industries and sizes
- Test and evaluate IT General Controls (ITGCs) across client environments, documenting findings and providing actionable remediation recommendations
- Support PCI DSS, HITRUST, HIPAA, and CMMC Level 2 compliance assessments as client workload requires
- Prepare and review audit workpapers, evidence requests, control narratives, and client-facing deliverables to a consistent standard of quality
- Work directly with clients to identify and assess information security risks, develop security policies and procedures, and provide practical remediation guidance
- Contribute to incident response planning, tabletop exercises, and business continuity engagements as part of Echelon's broader advisory portfolio
- Manage multiple concurrent client engagements, balancing priorities and delivering quality results on schedule
- Build strong internal and client relationships through clear written and verbal communication, translating technical findings for both technical and non-technical audiences
- Stay current with evolving compliance frameworks, audit standards, and security threats to strengthen client services and internal methodologies
- Demonstrate thought leadership by creating content for the organization's website and blog, and through involvement in the cybersecurity community

Your Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

- 2–4 years of hands-on experience in IT audit, compliance, or GRC consulting, with a focus on SOC 2 Type I/II audits, ISO 27001 assessments, or related attestation engagements
- Demonstrated understanding of IT General Controls (ITGCs), Trust Services Criteria, and audit standards such as SSAE 18 or ISAE 3402, with additional exposure to incident response planning and business continuity concepts.
- Ability to conduct risk assessments, compliance reviews, and readiness evaluations across frameworks, including SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, HITRUST, and HIPAA
- Strong analytical skills with the ability to identify and assess complex risk scenarios and offer practical solutions
- Familiarity with leading GRC tools and technologies to support compliance and risk management initiatives
- Excellent communication and presentation skills, capable of articulating technical concepts to technical and non-technical audiences
- Strong project management skills, including managing multiple engagements and deliverables simultaneously while maintaining high quality and client satisfaction standards
- Prior experience at a Big 4 firm, a mid-tier CPA/advisory firm, or a boutique IT audit/attestation firm is strongly preferred
- Applicants must have authorization to work in the United States without current or future visa sponsorship.

Preferred Qualifications

- Already certified in, or currently pursuing, one or more of the following: CISA, CIA, CPA, CISSP, and/or ISO 27001 Lead Auditor
- Experience with the incident response lifecycle
- Experience developing project plans and timelines
- Track record of high-volume SOC 2 or ISO 27001 engagement delivery in a client-facing consulting or attestation role
- Exposure to FedRAMP, CMMC, or other government compliance frameworks

Why Echelon? We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for our team with unquestioned integrity. If you have a special need that requires accommodation, please let your recruiter know. One of our core values is "People with Personality," and we want to allow you the space to bring your full self to work.We Currently Offer The Following Benefits

- Access to medical, dental, and vision insurance through Cigna, with the majority of the employee cost covered by the employer
- Employer funding to HSA accounts and FSA access
- Access to a 401(k) through Vanguard with a guaranteed employer contribution
- Flexible vacation policy that allows you to manage your schedule and rest and recharge when you need to.
- 11 holidays with flexibility based on what is important for you and those you love
- Employer-paid short-term and long-term disability, employer-paid life insurance, and access to additional life insurance, hospital coverage, accidental coverage, discounted mental health support, and more.
- Support for individual development through certifications, continued learning, conferences, and more

We value a diverse workforce and a culture of inclusivity and belonging. All employment decisions shall be made without regard to age, race, creed, color, religion, gender, national origin, ancestry, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetic information, marital status, citizenship status, or any other basis as protected by federal, state, or local law. title: Andreea Negrea - Global Data Privacy Manager | LinkedIn
description:
# Andreea Negrea

Global Data Privacy Manager

Romania (RO)

500 connections • 751 followers

## About

Senior privacy professional with over 9 years of progressive experience designing and leading global data protection programmes across complex, multinational organisations. I translate the intersection of emerging regulation — GDPR, EU AI Act, Cyber Resilience Act, NIS2, PIPL, and US state privacy laws — into scalable, business-aligned compliance frameworks that hold up under regulatory scrutiny. My work spans the full privacy lifecycle: strategic programme architecture, cross-border data governance, product privacy (privacy by design), incident response, DPIAs, vendor due diligence, works council engagement, and team leadership. I have deep hands-on experience with OneTrust (ROPA, Assessment Automation, Consent, Maturity & Planning) and have built privacy functions from the ground up within large industrial and technology organizations operating across EU, APAC, IMEA, China, and the Americas. I work closely with engineering and product teams on data architecture decisions, engaging directly with regulators and works councils. I am drawn to roles where privacy is treated as a strategic function — whether in-house, within an international organization, or in an advisory capacity.

Total Experience: 11 years and 1 month

## Experience

### [Copeland](https://www.linkedin.com/company/copeland)

#### Global Data Privacy Manager (Current)

Dec 2024 - Present (1 year and 7 months) in Cluj-Napoca

Lead the global data protection function for a multinational HVACR technology company with operations across 30+ jurisdictions. Responsible for strategic privacy governance, regulatory compliance, and cross-functional privacy integration across business units and geographies. Architecting Copeland's FY27 global privacy strategy spanning ROPA governance, the EU regulatory compliance roadmap (EU AI Act, NIS2, CRA), Privacy by Design for connected product lines, and OneTrust programme coordination. title: I did the math. It should make you angry. | Amy Hwang
description:
# I did the math. It should make you angry. | Amy Hwang · LinkedIn · 2026-03-28

**Amy Hwang**: N.Asia Sales Development at Deel with 10 years 2 months of experience. Previous roles include Regional Director at Quhuo, CKA Sales Manager at Alibaba Group, and Sales Director at BOSS直聘. Based in Beijing, China [CN].

---

I did the math. It should make you angry.
Average daily commute in Beijing: 3 hours. Round trip. 250 working days a year. That's 750 hours.

750 hours.
Enough to read 100 books. Become fluent in a new language. Go from zero to genuinely competent in an entirely new field.
And most office workers in Beijing hand that time over. Every single year.
Without thinking about it.

I've been working remotely for over two years now.
No commute. No clock-in. No meetings that exist because someone needed to fill a calendar slot.
Every morning I finish my workout, sit down, and start working. That's it. No hour lost before the day even begins.
And I put that time back into myself.
Every week. Without exception.

The result? Concrete. Compounding. Impossible to fake.
This is what people get wrong about remote work. 👇
The conversation always goes to flexibility.

Freedom. Work-life balance.
Those things are real. But they're not the point.
The point is 750 hours a year that are either working for you — or being handed to someone else's agenda.

In a knowledge-based career, that gap doesn't stay flat.
It compounds. Just not always in your favor.

What would you do with 750 hours a year — if you got them back?

![I did the math. It should make you angry. | Amy Hwang image](https://media.licdn.com/dms/image/v2/D5622AQE3PuVpoyFZpQ/feedshare-shrink_2048_1536/B56Z0yAlcaKwAg-/0/1774660507647?e=2147483647&v=beta&t=FEL75NdTn5sDO0YKKdCQm3-AuhyeE-O74yawT9F8fts)

title: 🚀 We're Hiring: GRC & Cybersecurity Intern | Ownux Global
description:
# 🚀 We're Hiring: GRC & Cybersecurity Intern | Ownux Global · LinkedIn · 2026-06-02

**Ownux Global**: Ownux Global is a leading cyber security penetration testing services company in Ahmedabad, India. They offer services like Web App Testing, Mobile App Testing, and Security Testing. Ownux Global has 10-20 employees (+7-8% YoY). Headquartered in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. Its workforce is distributed across India and United States.

---

🚀 We're Hiring: GRC & Cybersecurity Intern

📍 Location: Ahmedabad
💼 Internship Type: Full-time Internship

🔐 About the Role

Are you passionate about cybersecurity, compliance, and risk management?

Join our team as a GRC & Cybersecurity Intern and gain hands-on experience helping organizations strengthen their security posture and meet compliance requirements. This internship is an excellent opportunity for students and fresh graduates looking to build a career in Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC).

You'll work alongside experienced cybersecurity professionals, contribute to real-world projects, and learn industry-leading frameworks and standards.

🛠️ Key Responsibilities

- Assist in security assessments and compliance gap analyses
- Support ISO 27001, SOC 2, HIPAA, and other compliance initiatives
- Help document cybersecurity policies, procedures, and standards
- Participate in risk assessments and vendor security reviews
- Assist with audit preparation and evidence collection
- Research cybersecurity regulations, frameworks, and best practices
- Support incident response planning and security awareness initiatives
- Prepare reports, presentations, and compliance documentation

🎯 Required Skills & Qualifications

- Pursuing or recently completed a degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field
- Basic understanding of cybersecurity concepts and information security principles
- Familiarity with frameworks such as ISO 27001, NIST CSF, or CIS Controls is a plus
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
- Good written and verbal communication skills
- Ability to learn quickly and work collaboratively in a team environment
- Knowledge of networking, cloud security, or risk management concepts is an advantage

What You'll Gain

- Hands-on experience with real-world cybersecurity and compliance projects
- Exposure to industry standards and security frameworks
- Mentorship from experienced cybersecurity consultants
- Opportunity to work with clients across multiple industries
- Access to modern security tools and technologies
- Professional development and learning opportunities
- Potential full-time career opportunities based on performance
- Collaborative and growth-focused work environment
🍿 Free snacks!

📩 Apply Now

Send your resume to: palak@ownuxglobal.com

Start your cybersecurity journey with us and gain practical experience in Governance, Risk & Compliance while working on impactful security projects.

岗位职责1. 安全战略与体系建设

- 负责制定公司整体网络安全战略、中长期发展规划及年度实施计划。

- 负责安全预算的编制与管理，评估并引入合适的安全产品与服务。

- 管理防火墙、IDS/IPS、WAF、EDR、DLP、SOC等安全平台的策略优化与告警分析。

3. 合规与审计

- 配合内外部审计，完成安全合规检查，推动发现问题的整改闭环。

4. 业务安全赋能

- 参与公司IT项目（云迁移、新系统上线、办公网改造）的安全评审，提出架构安全建议。
- 负责供应链安全管理，审核第三方供应商的安全资质与合同条款。

任职资格1. 基本条件

- 本科及以上学历，计算机、网络安全、信息安全等相关专业。
- 5年以上网络安全工作经验，其中至少3年以上安全团队管理经验（或担任过大型项目的技术Lead）。
- 独立主导过中大型企业的安全体系从0到1建设者优先。

2. 专业技能

- 技术深度： 精通主流安全技术（防火墙、WAF、EDR、SOC、态势感知等），熟悉ATT&CK攻击框架；熟悉至少一种脚本语言（Python/Shell/Go）用于自动化安全运营。
- 攻防视角： 熟悉OWASP Top 10原理与防御，具备渗透测试实战能力或拥有CISP-PTE/OSCP认证者优先。
- 云安全： 熟悉主流公有云（AWS/阿里云/腾讯云）的安全产品配置与云安全架构（CSPM、CWPP）。
- 合规标准： 深入理解等级保护2.0、ISO 27001、GDPR或PCI-DSS，有主导过等保测评或ISO27001认证全流程经验者优先。

3. 软实力

- 危机处理： 在面对勒索病毒、数据泄露等紧急事件时，能保持冷静并做出快速、准确的决策。
- 沟通协作： 能向非技术背景的高管（CEO/董事会）清晰汇报安全风险与投入产出比，具备跨部门（法务、运维、研发）推动能力。
- 学习能力： 对新型攻击手法（如AI对抗、供应链攻击）保持高度敏感。

#### 公司介绍

北京领雁智远科技有限公司（简称“领雁智远”）成立于2022年10月，总部位于北京市西城区金融科技示范园区，注册资本4,000万元人民币，是北京领雁科技股份有限公司（原中信网络科技股份有限公司）设立的专业子公司。公司设有1个研发中心和4个实施中心。公司专注于人工智能产品与智能风控解决方案，自主创新研发了AI工程化产品，深耕大数据分析、人工智能技术应用领域，为银行、保险、证券等金融机构，以及央企、国企和大中型企业，提供专业的产品与解决方案。公司是国家高新技术企业，并已获评北京市“专精特新”中小企业。公司目前已累计获得软件著作权41项、注册商标35项，主要产品包括知汇魔擎（AI AgentsBase Platform，ABP）、知汇大禹审计系统、知汇九鼎合规系统及模型资产管理系统等。依托人工智能产品ABP，公司助力企业客户业务流程的智能化；其中，ABP已获得市场认可与客户青睐，成为客户在人工智能基础建设领域的重要选择；知汇大禹审计系统以前瞻的设计和卓越的用户体验赢得市场广泛认可，连续多年在银行业IT解决方案审计细分领域保持市场占有率领先；知汇九鼎合规系统与模型资产管理系统，也已成为众多客户的首要选择。

合规管理总监 50-70k·15薪

北京-海淀区 5-10年 统招本科 招1人 4月3日更新

微信分享扫码

五险一金 年终奖金 带薪年假 年度旅游 团队聚餐 节日礼物 优秀员工奖 定期体检 扁平管理 发展空间大

任女士 13小时前在线 已认证

职位介绍 一、 职位概述​ 作为法务与合规团队的核心成员，直接支持供应链采购，尤其侧重于应对日益复杂的国际贸易管制环境，并为高速增长的云计算业务提供全方位法律支持。 二、 主要职责​ 1、负责算力中心建设涉及的相关日常法务支持，包括业务运营涉及的软硬件采购、算力服务订阅，负责相关合同的起草、审阅、谈判等。 2、复杂云服务业务合作模式设计并协助落地，确保采购、研发、销售全链条符合监管要求，防范重大合规风险。 3、主导建立并持续优化符合美国EAR、中国《出口管制法》等多法规的全球贸易合规体系，包括物项分类、禁运筛查、内控流程与培训。 4、负责处理业务线涉及的诉前争议解决、能够独立处理诉讼案件。 5、推动法律与合规工作的智能化，探索并引入AI等工具，提升合同审查、合规筛查及知识管理的效率与精度。 三、 任职要求​ 1、全日制统招本科以上学历，法学专业，通过司法考试，有扎实的法律功底和良好的职业习惯。 2、5-10年以上法律相关工作经验，能够独立支持业务需求，英语可作为工作语言。 3、熟悉美国出口管制（EAR）、中国《出口管制法》相关法规和实务，具备大型硬件采购、技术服务或云计算合同的全程处理经验。 4、能深入理解AI算力、数据中心等业务逻辑，从业务增长与风险平衡角度提供解决方案。 5、具备严谨的逻辑判断和分析能力，善于思考、梳理、总结，具备出色的内外部沟通协调能力，能独立负责跨部门合规或合同专项，推动复杂流程落地。 其他信息 语言要求：英语、普通话 行业要求：AI/互联网/IT

## 公司简介

金山云，创立于2012年，中国知名的独立云服商。业务范围遍及全球多个国家和地区。成立8年来，金山云始终坚持以客户为中心的服务理念，提供安全、可靠、稳定、高品质的云计算服务。 当前，金山云已经构建了完备的云计算基础架构和运营体系，并通过与人工智能、大数据、物联网、区块链、边缘计算、AR/VR等优势技术的有机结合，提供适用于政务、金融、AIoT、医疗、工业、传媒、视频、游戏、教育、互联网等行业的解决方案。 当前，金山云已经在北京、上海、广州、杭州、扬州、天津等国内地区，以及俄罗斯、新加坡、美国等国际区域设有绿色节能数据中心及运营机构。未来，金山云将持续开展国际化战略，通过构建一张覆盖全球的云计算网络，连通更多设备和人群，让云计算的价值惠及全球。

职位介绍 职位描述： 你来解决什么问题 水滴公司目前在日常工作中已经大量引入AI Agent进行协同办公，我们希望找到一个人，在未来规模继续扩大之前，把Agent的安全规范、风险管控、技术防线等安全基础设施系统性地建起来。 你将负责： 1、主导AI Agent安全体系从0到1建设，包含网络安全、数据安全等维度； 2、通过技术手段识别和管控安全风险——权限边界设计、数据流管控、异常行为检测，不仅是靠规范文件约束； 3、持续识别员工使用agent过程中的安全薄弱点，输出技术评估和管控方案 以小组协作方式推进安全能力建设，统筹分工。 职位要求： 我们在找什么样的人： 1、资深研发背景，有安全领域真实项目经验（信息安全 / 数据安全 / 权限认证管控等方向均可）； 2、有企业级安全体系建设经验，且对AI agent风险有系统性认知——理解提示词注入、权限滥用与越权、沙箱隔离等Agent场景的安全风险和防范手段； 3、熟悉企业数据安全管控的常用方法； 4、深度理解LLM / agent原理； 5、有小团队管理经验优先。 加分项 1、大型互联网公司安全方向，或AI原生公司安全 / 治理岗背景 2、有企业级AI安全治理完整落地经历 AI能力要求 agent是你的日常主力工具，不是偶尔用一下。我们要的不是会用工具，而是真正理解agent在企业场景下的能力边界——哪里能放、哪里必须管、为什么——能把安全认知和实际使用结合起来。 为什么值得考虑 1、水滴员工AI工具使用率在互联网公司里属于头部，这个岗位面对的是真实、规模化的问题，不是务虚； 2、从零建体系，有完整的主导空间； 3、直接参与公司AI治理决策链。 其他信息 行业要求：全部行业

## 公司简介

水滴公司是中国保险和健康服务科技平台，创建于2016年4月，以“用互联网科技助推广大人民群众有保可医，保障亿万家庭”为使命，我们通过医疗筹款、保险平台以及健康服务平台构建了一个庞大的保险保障和健康服务网络，为用户提供健康保障解决方案。2021年5月，水滴公司登陆美国纽约证券交易所成功上市，股票代码“WDH” 水滴公司创建的“大病筹款+人身保险”的健康保障模式，提升了救急、救难的救助效率，在医保之外形成了多条医疗资金供给的有效补充渠道，成功地满足了覆盖整个社会阶层范围的多元化用户群的需求，建立了闭环医疗支付生态系统。 水滴公司还通过水滴好药付、水滴健康业务，从健康端为用户提供问诊、用药等健康服务。我们希望寻求机会加强与医院、医药公司等医疗服务伙伴的合作，建立一套“保险+健康服务“完善的健康生态系统。 水滴公司业务简介 水滴保 水滴保是水滴公司2017年5月推出的互联网保险经纪平台，运营主体为水滴保险经纪有限公司，是中国银保监会批复的全国性保险经纪公司。公司一直以“用互联网科技助推广大人民群众有保可医，保障亿万家庭”为使命，以“帮助用户优选高性价比保险产品”为服务理念。截至2021年3月，水滴保与62家保险公司合作，提供超过240款健康和寿险产品，覆盖医疗、重疾、意外、寿险、年金等人身健康险各类险种，为成人、少儿、老人以及慢病人群提供全方位的保障和服务；平台累计保障用户覆盖国内97%以上的市县，76%的用户来自小城镇及农村地区。根据调研数据显示，90%的用户通过水滴保完成个人在线投保，复购意愿高达73%。 水滴筹 水滴筹是国内个人大病求助互联网服务平台，也是国内互联网个人大病筹款0 服务费的开创者。截至 2021 年 3 月，约 3.6 亿的爱心人士通过水滴筹累计向近190 万名患者赠与了超过400亿医疗资金。水滴筹通过移动互联网技术将民间“互助互济”的线下行为搬到社交网络上，并通过亲友分享、移动支付等方式帮助陷入困境的大病患者及家庭更便捷地发布、传播求助信息，让赠与人也可以更方便地进行帮扶。

# Navigating China's Personal Data Export Compliance: Insights from MNC's Successful Application for Security Assessment
* [Report this article](https://www.linkedin.com/uas/login?session_redirect=https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/navigating-chinas-personal-data-export-compliance-insights-tfl8c&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_ellipsis-menu-semaphore-sign-in-redirect&guestReportContentType=PONCHO_ARTICLE&_f=guest-reporting)

### AnJie Broad Law Firm
#### AnJie Broad Law Firm is a leading PRC law firm providing full services to both international and domestic clients.
Published Mar 20, 2025
[+ Follow](https://www.linkedin.com/signup/cold-join?session_redirect=/pulse/navigating-chinas-personal-data-export-compliance-insights-tfl8c&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_publisher-author-card)
## Author: Albert Tsui, Partner
China’sPersonal Information Protection Law (“PIPL”), enacted in 2021, establishes a structured regulatory framework for cross-border transfers ofpersonal information(“PI”). Depending on the volume, sensitivity and context of PI being exported, exporters may face varying levels of compliance obligations. For instance, small-scale exports of non-sensitive PI may be exempt from formal applications to theCyberspace Administration of China(“CAC”), while larger or more sensitive transfers may require a CAC-prepared standard PI transfer contract(“Standard Contract”)or a CAC-organized data security assessment(“Data Security Assessment”).
Formultinational corporations (“MNCs”)operating in China, navigating these requirements can seem daunting. However, with the right approach, compliance is achievable and manageable.
We recently supported an MNC in successfully securing an approval for a Data Security Assessment. Through the application process, we gained firsthand experience in engaging with both provincial and national levels of CAC. This was a valuable opportunity to better understand CAC’s approach to exercising its authority under the PIPL and its interpretation of relevant regulations.
Notably, the number of successfully completed Data Security Assessments remains relatively low (only 285 as of December 2024), making this experience particularly rare and insightful.
This article summarizes our experience and provides a guide to key aspects of cross-border PI compliance, focusing on:
1. Understanding the key regulatory requirements for PI export
2. Identifying the appropriate level of compliance through a data audit
3. Preparing for the impact assessment and application with CAC
4. Maintaining post-approval compliance
1.  Understanding the Regulatory Landscape: A Moving Target
PIPL provides the legal foundation for cross-border PI transfers, but the regulatory environment continues to evolve. Key requirements under PIPL Article 38 include:
1.Passing a CAC-organized Data Security Assessment.
2. Signing a CAC-Standard Data Transfer Contract with the overseas recipient.
3. Obtaining PI protection certification from a professional institution.
Condition 3 (certification) is a less commonly used. Our focus is on Conditions 1 (Data Security Assessment) and 2 (Standard Contract).
When Standard Contracts are Required
TheMeasures for Personal Information Export Standard Contract (2022) (“Standard Contract Measures”)(Article 4) outline scenarios requiring a Standard Contract with foreign recipients and its filing with CAC, including:
* The exporter is not a Critical Information Infrastructure (CII) operators.
* Handling PI of fewer than 1 million individuals in China.
* Exporting sensitive PI of fewer than 10,000 individuals within a calendar year.
* Exporting non-sensitive PI of fewer than 100,000 individuals within a calendar year.
When Security Assessments Are Required
TheMeasures for Security Assessment of Data Exports (2022) (“Security Assessment Measures”)(Article 4) specify scenarios requiring mandatory CAC risk assessments, including:
* Exporting important data.
* CII operators or processors handling PI of over 1 million individuals.
* Exporting sensitive PI of 10,000 individuals or non-sensitive PI of 100,000 individuals within a calendar year.
Regulatory Relaxations Under the 2024 Provisions
TheProvisions on Promoting and Standardizing Cross-Border Data Flows (2024)(“the Provisions”) introduce exemptions to ease compliance burdens for certain categories of data transfers. Businesses falling under these categories are exempt from Security Assessments or Standard Contracts:
1. Contractual necessity: For activities like cross-border shopping, payment processing, shipping, or services such as hotel bookings and visa applications.
2. Employment management: For cross-border human resource management, such as processing employee information for global payroll or benefits.
3. Emergency situations: To protect an individual's life, health, or property in emergencies.
4. Low-volume, non-sensitive transfers: Non-sensitive PI of fewer than 100,000 individuals annually.
These changes are consolidated in the Regulations on the Management of Network Data Security, enacted shortly after the Provisions. The table below summarizes the regulatory requirements before and after the relaxation:
![Article content]()
2. Conducting a Comprehensive Data Audit: The Cornerstone of Compliance
A successful compliance strategy begins with a detailed data audit, which involves:
* Evaluating thepurpose,volume, andsensitivityof PI exports.
* Assessing the security capabilities of both the exporter and the foreign recipient.
* Reviewing legal agreements to ensure alignment with regulatory requirements.
The first point is critical, as the three elements correspond to the three key determinants of compliance obligations imposed on MNCs:
●Purpose– The necessity of the PI export must be justified. Unnecessary PI cannot be exported.
●Volume– Higher volumes of PI exports trigger stricter compliance requirements. For example, an MNC handling PI of over 1 million individuals must undergo a Data Security Assessment, even if exporting just one piece of PI.

●Sensitivity– MNCs can now benefit from the Provisions and export more PI. But sensitive PI exports are subject to stricter rules. Even a very small volume of sensitive PI export may require a Standard Contract.
If PI is deemed sensitive and the export volume reaches certain thresholds, the MNC must arrange a correspondingSecurity AssessmentorStandard Contractto be filed with CAC.The MNC must also justify the necessity of the PI export, often by demonstrating how the transfer is essential to its business operations. Common justifications include:
• Global customer relationship management (e.g., membership systems).
• Cross-border analytics to improve customer experiences.
• Compliance with international legal or contractual obligations.
3. Preparing PIPIA and CAC application: Building a Strong Justification
Even if an exemption under the Provisions applies, MNCs are not waived from preparingPersonal Information Protection Impact Assessment (“PIPIA”)to document compliance efforts. After the data audit, if an MNC determines that a CAC application is not required, it is advisable to engage a reputable, independent and domestic third party to prepare a PIPIA. This serves as a critical record in case of future regulatory challenges.
If no exemption applies, the next step is determining whether to pursue a Standard Contract or a Security Assessment. Under the Provisions, non-sensitive PI benefits from relaxed thresholds, allowing annual exports of up to 1 million individuals' data under a Standard Contract. In contrast, sensitive PI exports remain strictly regulated. Exporting sensitive PI of even one individual requires a Standard Contract, while exports exceeding 10,000 individuals annually trigger a mandatory Data Security Assessment.
Accurate classification PI is therefore pivotal. Misclassification could lead to unnecessary assessments or, worse, regulatory non-compliance.
According to PIPL Article 28, sensitive PI is defined as data that, if leaked or misused, could harm an individual's dignity, personal safety, or property. This includes:
* Biometric data
* Religious beliefs
* Political opinions
* Health and medical information
* Financial account details
* Location tracking data
* Information about minors under 14 years old
If an MNC exports sensitive PI of between 1-9999 individuals in a calendar year, a Standard Contract must be signed with its overseas recipient, usually its headquarters outside China. Since the terms are standard, the application process is straightforward, requiring submission of the signed contract and a PIPIA to the provincial CAC. Approval typically takes 10 working days.
For exports exceeding 10,000 sensitive PI individuals annually, a Security Assessment is required. The MNC must submit the following documents to the provincial CAC, which will forward them to the national CAC for approval:
-       Application form
-       Data Export Risk Self-Assessment Report
-       Data contract between exporter and foreign recipient
-       Other supporting materials as required
National CAC is legally required to complete the assessment within 45 working days from a formal acceptance. But prior to it, MNCs should expect to respond to multiple rounds of inquiries from both provincial and national CACs.
4. Embracing Post-approval Compliance: A Continuous Journey
Securing PI export approval is a significant milestone, but the journey doesn't end there. Both Security Assessment Measures and Standard Contract Measures stipulate that any changes to the conditions recorded in the CAC application require a new application. Additionally, a Security Assessment is valid for only two years, requiring renewal even if no changes occur.
MNCs are encouraged to take the following measures to ensure full and continuous compliance with PIPL:
* Implement Ongoing Risk Monitoring:Establish mechanisms for continuously monitoring data security risks and promptly addressing any emerging threats.
* Conduct Regular Security Audits:Periodically assess data security posture to identify and rectify vulnerabilities.
* Invest in Robust Security Technologies:Leverage encryption, data masking, and access control technologies to safeguard data.
* Cultivate a Culture of Security Awareness:Regularly train employees on data security best practices.
Conclusion: MNC’s PI Compliance in China is Achievable and Manageable
While China’s PI export regulations may appear stringent, they are designed to protect individuals’ privacy without unduly burdening businesses. Recent relaxations under the Provisions demonstrate a pragmatic approach to balancing security and business needs.
For MNCs, successful compliance hinges on:
* Understanding regulatory requirements and staying updated on changes.
* Conducting thorough data audits to determine the appropriate level of compliance.
* Engaging proactively with CAC authorities to address inquiries and justify data export activities.
Our experience assisting an MNC through the Data Security Assessment process underscores that compliance is both achievable and manageable with the right preparation and expertise. By adopting a structured approach and leveraging professional guidance, MNCs can confidently navigate China’s data export regulations and ensure their operations remain compliant and secure.
In short, while the process requires effort, it is far from insurmountable. With clear guidelines, practical exemptions, and a collaborative approach, MNCs can successfully meet China’s personal information compliance requirements and continue to thrive in one of the world’s most dynamic markets.

# The Clock is Ticking: 3 Months Left to Adopt the China SCCs for Cross-border Data Transfer
* [Report this article](https://www.linkedin.com/uas/login?session_redirect=https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/clock-ticking-3-months-left-adopt-china-sccs-cross-border-zhu&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_ellipsis-menu-semaphore-sign-in-redirect&guestReportContentType=PONCHO_ARTICLE&_f=guest-reporting)
[Yingying Zhu](https://cn.linkedin.com/in/yingying-zhu-a2790850)![Yingying Zhu]()
### Yingying Zhu
#### Partner at Beijing Mingdun Law Firm
Published Sep 6, 2023
[+ Follow](https://www.linkedin.com/signup/cold-join?session_redirect=/pulse/clock-ticking-3-months-left-adopt-china-sccs-cross-border-zhu&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_publisher-author-card)
Introduction
The China Standard Contractual Clauses (hereinafter the “China SCCs”) as well as the application rules have been promulgated by the Cyberspace Administration of China (hereinafter the “CAC”) on February, 24, 2023, and have become effective on June 1, 2023.
The CAC offers a six-month grace period for personal information handlers[[1]](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=#_edn1&urlhash=T6aV&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)(hereinafter the “PI Handlers”) to take necessary measures to comply with the requirements for their cross-border transfer of Personal Information (hereinafter the “PI”), which will end on November 30, 2023, therefore only three months are left to incorporate the China SCCs into the current data transfer provisions, and the clock is ticking.
“The Trio”
According to Article 38 of thePersonal Information Protection Law of the People’s Republic of China(hereinafter the “PIPL”)[[2]](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=#_edn2&urlhash=fSj3&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block), effective on November 1st, 2021, for PI Handler (i.e., the “Data Exporter”) who is to transfer PI to an entity located outside of China (i.e., the “Overseas Recipient”), the first thing should be made sure is that they have adopted one of the following three mechanisms:
1. Pass a security assessment administered by CAC, which is compulsory if the PI Handlers’ data processing activities are falling into one of the following four categories:
(1) Processing PI as a Critical Information Infrastructure Operators[[3]](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=#_edn3&urlhash=h6Zz&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)(hereinafter the “CIIO”);
(2) Processing PI of more than 1 million PRC residents;
(3) Transferring PI of more than 100,000 PRC residents abroad in the preceding year; or
(4) Transferring sensitive PI of more than 10,000 PRC residents abroad in the preceding year.
For all the other PI Handlers not falling into one of the above four categories, they can choose one of the measures prescribed in the below:
2. Obtain a PI protection certification issued by professional institutions pursuant to CAC regulations, or
3. Conclude an agreement with the Overseas Recipient based on the China SCCs for the PI transfers.
The release of the China SCCs as well as the application rules completes the last missing piece for “the Trio” and it provides a meaningful and time efficient mechanism for PI Handlers to transfer PI outside of China, if, of course, they are neither the CIIOs nor entities processing a certain threshold amount of PI as listed in the above.
Akin to the EU SCCs under the GDPR?
While sharing some similarities with the EU SCCs in setting forth the rights and obligations of the Data Exporter and the Overseas Recipient and requiring the Overseas Recipient to apply security measures (both technical and organizational) to safeguard the PI transferred, the China SCCs demonstrate some of the unique Chinese characteristics:
1. One Template Fits all
While the EU SCCs have a modular approach, include general clauses applicable to all cases and four modules tailored to the capacity in which the parties will be using the personal data and the parties have to choose the module that reflects their situation (i.e., if they are a controller, processor or a sub-processor) and whether they are a data exporter or a data importer,[[4]](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=#_edn4&urlhash=b1Qg&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)the China SCCs generally describe the obligations of the Data Exporter and the Overseas Recipient in one uniformed template.
In a nutshell, the reason could be explained as follows: the GDPR distinguishes the roles of the data controller and data processor, while the PIPL only defines the role of the PI handler (which is akin to “data controller” under the GDPR) but not data processor (which is referred to under Article 59 of the PIPL as the “Entrusted Party”). Under the PIPL, most direct obligations apply to PI Handlers, while obligations on Entrusted Parties are not clearly prescribed by the law. As commonly understood, the obligations of the Entrusted Parties largely arise based on contractual obligations imposed on these entities by the PI Handlers. This explains that as an extension of the PIPL, the China SCCs only have one uniformed template, without distinguishing the obligations of the parties based on their relationship or their roles and functions in the transfers of PI.
2.The Governing Law
Under the China SCCs, the establishment, validity, performance,  and the interpretation of the contract and any disputes arising from the contract shall be governed by the relevant laws and regulations of China, while in the EU SCCs, under the data transfer scenarios of controller-to-controller, controller-to-processor, and processor-to-processor, the governing law could be the law of one of the EU Member States allowing for third-party beneficiary rights, chosen by the parties, and under the scenario of processor-to-controller, the governing law could be the law of any country allowing for third-party beneficiary rights, chosen by the parties.

3. Filing Obligation
The China SCCs shall be filed with the provincial CAC for recordation within 10 working days upon their execution. At the same time, a PI protection impact assessment report shall be submitted as part of the recordation documents. Nevertheless, whether or not the recordation is filed with the provincial CAC will not affect the validity of the China SCCs executed between the parties.
In the case of the EU SCCs, they can be used by Data Exporters, without the need to obtain a prior authorization (for the data transfer or the clauses used) from a data protection authority.[[5]](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=#_edn5&urlhash=J8MB&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)
4. Onward Transfers of PI
Under the China SCCs, PI can only be further transferred to third parties by the Overseas Recipient if the following requirements are all well met:
1)     There are true commercial needs for the PI’s onward transfers;
2)     The PI subjects have been duly informed;
3)     Where the processing of PI is based on individual consent, the individual’s separate consent should be obtained;
4)     The third parties have been obligated by a contract offering an adequate level of PI protection as the China SCCs;
5)     The prior consent of the PI Handler should be secured; and
6)     The PI processing activities of the third parties should be supervised.
5. No Alteration
Except for the optional choices left to the parties under the specific clauses, such as the choices for the place of arbitration, the China SCCs shall be accepted as a whole when being incorporated by the parties as part of their agreement who could only decide supplementary terms of their agreement, provided that those supplemented terms are not conflicting with the China SCCs.
While under the EU SCCs, if the parties change the text of the SCCs themselves (i.e. beyond choosing the relevant modules and/or options and filling in square brackets and annexes), the modified clauses may no longer be used as a basis for data transfers to third countries, unless they are approved by a national data protection authority as “ad hoc clauses” (pursuant to Article 46(3)(a) of the GDPR).[[6]](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=#_edn6&urlhash=yilH&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)
Conclusion
With specific PI protection safeguards to ensure that PI are adequately protected when transferring outside of China, the China SCCs could be well utilized as a convenient tool for cross-border PI transfers, if the PI Handler, i.e., the Data Exporter, is not falling within the four prescribed categories where the use of the China SCCs would not be an option.
Given the significance and timeline (only three months left) for mandatory adoption of the China SCCs, if not already done so, businesses with data flows in and outside of China are advised to immediately take actions to 1) obtain a proper English translation of the China SCCs from a trustworthy source; 2) comprehend the China SCCs and understand their differences with the EU SCCs; 3) determine whether any existing technical and organizational practices will be impacted; 4) find out whether the important business partners in China belong to the four prescribed categories and whether they understand the application rules of the China SCCs; and 5) review, re-negotiate, draft, and update agreements, protocols, policies and procedures where and if necessary.
[[1]](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=#_ednref1&urlhash=lJzH&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)PI Handlers determine the purpose and means of processing of PI and operate in a way similar to “data controllers” under other privacy and data protection laws (e.g., the European Union’s General Data Protection Regulation (2016/679) (“GDPR”).
[[2]](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=#_ednref2&urlhash=P-tP&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)On November 1st, 2021, China’s first comprehensive data privacy law, thePersonal Information Protection Law of the People’s Republic of China(the “PIPL”), has become effective. The PIPL basically requires that the operators of websites, mobile phone applications or any other technologies doing data collection and processing should obtain consent from users or have other legitimate basis in order to collect/process the users’ PI.
[[3]](https://www.linkedin.com/redir/redirect?url=#_ednref3&urlhash=OTaj&trk=article-ssr-frontend-pulse_little-text-block)Critical information infrastructure operators or entities processing a certain threshold amount of PI, will be required store PI domestically. If it is necessary for they to transfer such PI overseas, the data processor must pass a security assessment administered by CAC. “Critical information infrastructure” (normally referred to as “CII”) means any of network facilities and information systems in important industries and fields—such as public communication and information services, energy, transportation, water conservancy, finance, public services, e-government, and science, technology and industry for national defense.

# 🔒 How Remote Work Has Changed Cybersecurity for African Companies, And What To Do About It | Sumo-compliance automation · LinkedIn · 2025-06-18

**Sumo-compliance automation**: Sumo-compliance automation has 20-30 employees (1-2% YoY decline). Its workforce is distributed across Uganda, Kenya, and United States.

---

🔒 How Remote Work Has Changed Cybersecurity for African Companies, And What To Do About It

Remote work isn’t just a trend anymore, it’s how many businesses across Africa now operate, from growing startups to large corporates.

But while remote work boosts productivity and flexibility, it also opens new doors for cyber attackers.

Here’s what we’re seeing on the ground:
✅ More devices = more risk. Many employees use personal laptops and smartphones that lack robust security.
✅ Unsecured Wi-Fi. Home routers and coffee shop hotspots are easy targets for hackers.
✅ Cloud tools everywhere. Google Drive, Slack, Zoom — convenient, but misconfigured settings can leak sensitive company data.
✅ Phishing on the rise. Scammers know people are distracted at home. Fake emails pretending to be from IT or HR are spiking.
✅ Insider threats are harder to detect. Without physical oversight, it’s easy to overlook misuse of credentials or accidental leaks.

So what can African companies do to protect their teams and data?

🔑 Use company-managed devices whenever possible.
🔑 Require strong passwords and multi-factor authentication for all accounts.
🔑 Train staff regularly to spot phishing attempts.
🔑 Secure home routers and encourage VPN use.
🔑 Monitor cloud access and set clear permissions.
🔑 Have a clear incident response plan ready — before something happens.

✨ Remote work is here to stay. Your cyber risks don’t have to be.

We help African businesses secure remote teams, cloud data, and devices, without slowing down productivity.

👉 Our platform will be live soon, get ready to run a free website security audit and see what hackers see, before they do.

# This raises the bar for companies: compliance won’t come from moving data alone, but from understanding what that data actually is. Granular visibility into structure, sensitivity, and value is what makes data … | Bruno Raymond · LinkedIn · 2026-04-24

**Bruno Raymond**: Vice President at La French Tech Beijing with 26 years 3 months of experience. Previous roles include Senior Manager, Technical Program Management Lead - Data & Analytics at The Walt Disney Company, Senior Manager, Technical Program Management Lead - Data & Analytics at Hulu, and Business Operation Manager - Data & Analytics at Hulu. Based in Beijing, China [CN].

---

This raises the bar for companies: compliance won’t come from moving data alone, but from understanding what that data actually is. Granular visibility into structure, sensitivity, and value is what makes data residency and AI obligations actionable rather than reactive. The organizations that invest in deep data awareness will be the ones that can comply efficiently—and extract value at the same time.

> 👉Bottom line
> Nigeria is moving beyond GDPR-style frameworks into enforcement-driven digital industrial policy — where data control and value capture are both regulated.

title: Paula Cipierre
description:
# Paula Cipierre

Global Head of Privacy | LL.M. IT Law | Certified Privacy (CIPP/E & CIPP/A) and AI Governance Professional (AIGP)

Berlin, Berlin, Germany (DE)

500 connections • 9,865 followers

## About

For more than a decade, I've helped private and public organizations translate legal requirements into technical design and everyday organizational practice. I am a certified privacy professional (CIPP/E, CIPP/A, GDD cert. EU), ISO27001 information security auditor (TÜV Süd), and AI governance professional (AIGP). I am an expert in European data protection (GDPR) and AI law (AI Act). My goal is to help companies implement these laws in ways that advance their strategic objectives. I am passionate about engaging with the public on the ethics of big data and AI. I regularly run workshops on responsible AI, and speak at relevant conferences and events. I have published numerous articles about data law and policy, and have co-authored a book about what we can learn from art to shape the future with software. I seek meaningful connections with people that care deeply about the impact of technology on society. If you meet this description, feel free to reach out.

Total Experience: 16 years and 1 month

## Experience

Jul 2025 - Present (1 year) in Berlin, Germany

Leading a global team of subject-matter experts across EMEA, APAC, and AMS to facilitate privacy compliance across 60 countries and for more than 230,000 employees worldwide. Fostering the responsible development and deployment of AI as part of HCLTech's AI Ethics Committee. Actively collaborating with works councils to ensure new technologies are rolled out in a fair and transparent manner.

Department: Legal • Level: Head

### Not Tracking: The Antipolitics of Contact-Tracing Applications

In response to the COVID‐19 pandemic, governments around the world turned to contact‐tracing applications in an attempt to balance the reopening of the economy with keeping the virus at bay. But as this article demonstrates, contact‐tracing applications not only fail to protect the most vulnerable among us; they also shift responsibility for failing to prepare public‐health systems for a pandemic away from governments and onto the individual user struggling to contain its worst effects. In the process, contact‐tracing applications change the definition of failure. They also reinforce existing inequalities. Technology in this case not only has politics; it prevents politics. By focusing on contact‐tracing applications as an example, the article points to some of the deeper perils of accepting app‐based solutions to structural problems. ### Beware the Magic of Metrics

This article maps out the relationship between magic and metrics. It argues that metrics can be meaningful measures of progress, but that it’s important to remain aware of their limitations. Blind faith in metrics can mean that only that which is counted counts, but the hard part is knowing what to count, to begin with, and the extent to which we can count what counts. In the times of COVID-19, special care needs to be taken to avoid reading into the numbers what we most want to get out of them. Saviors, numerical or not, are often set up for failure – and the fall can be steep when the trust in government and trust in technology is already eroding. In mapping out the relationship between magic and metrics, we encourage the exploration of a more measured path out of this crisis, one that focuses less on how to return to normal, but first and foremost what normal is worth returning to. ### Power to Whom? Privacy in a Post-GDPR World - Jan 2019

In May 2018, the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) came into effect, the biggest reform of EU data protection law in over 20 years. While the GDPR introduced a number of important changes, it embodies the same core principles that have undergirded data protection law from the beginning. At the same time, due to its broad material and territorial scope as well as high potential fines for non-compliance, among others, the GDPR attracted an unprecedented amount of lobbying and media attention, turning a subject matter once considered niche into an unlikely battleground for political and economic influence. Those battles are far from settled. The lack of clarity surrounding the correct implementation of the law has left a power void that existing and emerging actors in the data protection landscape are eager to fill, and not only in Europe. The following contribution will outline the key actors involved in making and shaping the GDPR, the principles, rules and norms they are advancing, and what implications different implementations of the law might have on who sets the standards, both legal and technical, on how personal data is processed in the EU and beyond. ### On digital passages and borders: refugees and the new infrastructure for movement and control | Mark Latonero

Since 2014, millions of refugees and migrants have arrived at the borders of Europe. This article argues that, in making their way to safe spaces, refugees rely not only on a physical but increasingly also digital infrastructure of movement. Social media, mobile devices, and similar digitally networked technologies comprise this infrastructure of “digital passages”—sociotechnical spaces of flows in which refugees, smugglers, governments, and corporations interact with each other and with new technologies. At the same time, a digital infrastructure for movement can just as easily be leveraged for surveillance and control. European border policies, in particular, instantiate digital controls over refugee movement and identity. We review the actors, technologies, and policies of movement and control in the EU context and argue that scholars, policymakers, and the tech community alike should pay heed to the ethics of the use of new technologies in refugee and migration flows. ### Apple vs. FBI: Asking the right questions

The US government’s repeated attempts to force Apple to make the contents of its handheld devices accessible for law enforcement purposes has pitted two common conceptions of security against each other: computer security and national security. The government argues that current industry encryption standards seriously undermine its ability to engage in legitimate law enforcement and national security investigations. On the other hand, Apple argues that it cannot undermine the security of one iPhone without undermining the security of all iPhones. Ultimately, an evaluation of the trade-off between computer security and national security requires not only an analysis of what is legally possible but also what is politically and socially desirable. Such analysis, at the very minimum, requires engaging with the following four questions: first, are the government’s requests legitimate? Second, are the government’s requests lawful? Third, are the government’s requests reasonable? And fourth and finally, do the government’s requests make sense in light of what the government is ultimately trying to achieve? ### Bridging the transatlantic divide in privacy

In the context of the NSA surveillance scandal the transatlantic privacy divide has come back to the fore. In the United States, the right to privacy is primarily understood as a right to physical privacy, i.e. the protection from unwarranted government searches and seizures. In Germany on the other hand, it is also understood as a right to spiritual privacy, thus the right of citizens to develop into autonomous moral agents. More fundamentally, American and German attitudes towards privacy reflect different underlying constitutional assumptions: privacy as an aspect of liberty or as an aspect of dignity. As data flows defy jurisdictional boundaries, however , policymakers across the Atlantic are faced with a conundrum: how can German and American privacy cultures be reconciled? ### Metadata in Context – An Ontological and Normative Analysis of the NSA’s Bulk Telephony Metadata Collection Program | Helen Nissenbaum

In the aftermath of the Snowden revelations, the National Security Agency (NSA) responded to fears about warrantless domestic surveillance programs by emphasizing that it was collecting only the metadata, and not the content, of communications. When justifying its activities, the NSA offered the following rationale: because data involves content and metadata does not, a reasonable expectation of privacy extends only to the former but not the latter. Our paper questions the soundness of this argument. More specifically, we argue that privacy is defined not only by the types of information at hand, but also by the context in which the information is collected. This context has changed dramatically. Defining privacy as contextual integrity we are able, in the first place, to explain why the bulk telephony metadata collection program violated expectations of privacy and, in the second, to evaluate whether the benefits to national security provided by the program can be justified in light of the program's material costs, on the one hand, and its infringements on civil liberties, on the other hand.   >
  > In the article, the authors discuss the extent to which different legal bases for processing personal data under Art. 6(1) GDPR can be leveraged for training AI models:
  >
  > 1️⃣ Consent
  >
  > Consent is only a feasible legal basis for processing personal data to train AI models, if users can be informed transparently about the specific purpose of the processing and the circumstances of the data processing at the moment when the data is collected, and if the right of withdrawal can be exercised.
  >
  > In other words, consent is not a feasible option whenever the controller:
  > ❌ Does not have a direct relationship with the data subject
  > ❌ Cannot further specify the means and purposes of processing
  > ❌ Does not design the model training such that personal data can easily be removed
  >
  > 2️⃣ Contract
  >
  > Personal data can be processed under the #GDPR when it is necessary for the performance of a contract to which the data subject is party. Controllers can use this as the legal basis to process personal data for training AI models only if the processing is objectively necessary for the performance of the contract and in the absence of less intrusive alternatives. Alas, this will rarely be the case.
  >
  > 3️⃣ Legal obligation
  >
  > Personal data can be processed under the #GDPR whenever it is necessary to comply with a legal obligation to which the controller is subject. This, too, will be far-fetched in the case of training AI.
  >
  > 4️⃣ Legitimate interest
  >
  > Controllers could argue that processing personal data for training AI models constitutes a legitimate interest of theirs, if they are able to meet the following three-pronged test:
  >
  > ✅ The controller has a legitimate interest in processing personal data to train AI models indeed. Business interests are legitimate interests according to the #ECJ.
  > ✅ Processing personal data in that way is objectively necessarily.
  > ✅ The interests and rights of data subjects do not outweigh the legitimate interest of the controller.
  >
  > This, in turn, depends on the risks to data subjects, the extent to which the controller can mitigate those risks, and data subjects' reasonable expectations.
  >
  > 🚧 The situation is further complicated whenever the processing of special categories of personal data as defined by Art. 9(1) GDPR is involved, regardless of the intentions of the controller.
  >
  > 💡 As demonstrated by recent proceedings by the Verbraucherzentrale NRW against #Meta (https://bit.ly/4k2lYPb), processing personal data for training AI models is contentious.   > 2️⃣ Develop a system-level understanding of India's AI ecosystem.

description:
# A leading Chinese cybersecurity company is looking to hire an OT Penetration Tester to join the team in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, with potential travel across the MENA region. | Ismail Ahmed - 韦德 · LinkedIn · 2025-09-01

**Ismail Ahmed - 韦德**: CEO & Founder at Yalla Hack with 6 years 2 months of experience. Previous roles include Information Technology Officer at CMA CGM, Cybersecurity Researcher at HackerOne, and Network Engineering at FiberHome. Based in China [CN].

---

A leading Chinese cybersecurity company is looking to hire an OT Penetration Tester to join the team in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, with potential travel across the MENA region.

Key Responsibilities:
--> Perform vulnerability assessments and safe penetration testing across OT/ICS environments (PLCs, RTUs, DCS, HMIs).
--> Use OT-safe tooling and follow industrial safety processes (e.g., LOTO) to avoid operational disruption.
--> Review OT network architectures (e.g., Purdue Model) and validate segmentation between IT/OT zones.
--> Identify and safely exploit weaknesses in OT protocols (Modbus, DNP3, S7comm, OPC UA) and embedded firmware.
--> Collaborate with control system engineers to define secure test scopes, operational constraints, and rollback plans.
--> Translate technical findings into business and operational risks with clear mitigation recommendations.
--> Align assessments with IEC 62443, NIST SP 800-82, and ISO/IEC 27001 for OT.
--> Produce clear, actionable reports and briefings for engineering and executive stakeholders.

Qualifications:
--> Bachelor’s degree or higher in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
--> 3+ years of experience in OT security assessments, ICS penetration testing, or critical infrastructure defense.
--> Deep knowledge of ICS components (PLCs, RTUs, HMIs), Purdue Model architectures, and OT networking.
--> Proficiency with Wireshark (OT dissectors), Nessus/Tenable.ot, Metasploit (used cautiously), and GRFICS.
--> Familiarity with LOTO, MOC, and industrial safety processes.
--> Strong English communication and presentation skills. Arabic is a plus.
--> High sense of responsibility when working around production environments; strong stakeholder communication.
--> Information security certifications are a plus (GICSP, GRID, ICS410, ISA/IEC 62443, OSCP, CEH, PenTest+, CCNA).
--> Hands-on experience with WirelessHART/ISA100/LoRaWAN, Python/PowerShell scripting for ICS, OT incident response or physical security, and research/publications in OT threat analysis or protocol fuzzing are bonuses.
--> Experience working in the MENA region is a bonus.

To apply, please send your resume to:
cybersecurity_404@protonmail.ch
Subject: [Your Name] - [Current Residence] - OT Penetration Tester

If you're passionate about safeguarding industrial systems and have the skills we need, we’d love to hear from you!

### 职位描述

数据安全CISP-DSG安全评估

岗位职责 1、独立开展数据安全现状评估、合规差距分析、风险评估，严格依据相关国家标准、行业监管规范实施全流程评估；2、主导数据全生命周期安全核查，覆盖采集、存储、传输、使用、共享、销毁等各环节及应急处置；3、独立编制完整交付成果：数据安全评估报告、风险评估报告、整改方案、制度体系文件、PIA报告；4、统筹与各部门（如业务、安全、合规、法务等部门）的现场调研、技术检测与访谈沟通，识别核心/重要数据、敏感个人信息，识别重大安全风险与合规漏洞，给出可落地整改措施；5、对接客户IT、法务、业务部门，协助解决整改过程中的合规与技术问题，确保整改要求落地执行，验证整改效果，出具整改复核意见；6、指导初级顾问工作，审核交付物质量，把控项目进度；7、为客户提供常态化合规咨询、自查指导。技能要求1、掌握数据安全和个人信息保护领域法律法规以及GB/T 45577-2025、GB/T 37988-2019、GB/T 39335-2020、GB/T 45574-2025等国家标准和各行业数据安全相关标准，能够根据客户实际情况拆解合规要求；2、掌握数据安全风险评估、DSMM差距评估、个人信息保护影响评估、个人信息保护合规审计等原理，熟悉数据采集、存储、传输、处理、共享、销毁等各环节的合规要点，结合客户实际情况准确识别其中存在的安全风险；3、熟悉数据安全技术原理，了解市面上常见的数据安全产品及主要功能、适用场景、部署方式等；4、至少 5 年以上数据安全相关工作经验，参与数据安全评估项目不少于5个，具备一定的项目管理能力；5、具备优秀的沟通能力，能够与客户进行有效沟通，清晰准确地了解客户需求，获取项目所需信息；6、具备良好的文档撰写能力，能够按照要求编写规范、详实、准确的评估底稿和评估报告，逻辑清晰，表达流畅；7、持有持CISP、CISP-DSG、CDPSE、CDSP、CCRC-DSO、CISSP、DSMM测评师、数据安全评估师、CISP-PIP、个人信息保护合规审计人员、CCRC-PIPCA等专业资质至少1个。

#### 公司介绍

成都聚思亿科技有限公司位于成都高新区，专注于大数据处理、实时计算系统开发及企业级应用解决方案，业务涵盖物联网技术服务、人工智能应用开发与数字技术服务领域。公司依托Hadoop、Flink、Spark Streaming等技术栈，为多行业提供实时数仓建设、用户画像构建及分布式系统架构设计服务，在数据链路优化与高并发场景处理方面形成技术沉淀。技术团队深耕微服务架构与云化解决方案，具备Kubernetes容器化部署、Iceberg/Hudi数据湖技术及多组件协同开发经验。核心成员在大型系统架构设计、调度平台二次开发及华为DWS平台应用等领域拥有实践积累，持续强化实时数据处理与智能化服务能力。目前业务已拓展至昆明、贵阳等地区，为金融、能源等领域提供定制化技术服务。公司立足技术创新与工程实践融合，致力于通过高效节能技术研发与系统集成服务，推动企业数字化转型。未来将持续深化大数据实时计算与人工智能技术融合，拓展智慧城市、工业互联网等垂直场景应用，为技术人才提供参与前沿项目研发与跨区域协作的职业发展平台。

### 职位描述

数据安全法律合规咨询网络/信息安全法律服务咨询服务

基本情况： 年龄：28-35岁； 性别：不限； 学历：统招本科以上，排名靠前院校及研究生优先； 专业：计算机、软件、网络空间安全、法学、法律相关专业。 能力画像： 工作经验：5年以上工作经验（硕士3年即可），数据安全、数据合规领域至少2年工作经验，有数据出境风险自评估报告撰写经验。具有知名大型企业、咨询机构、研究机构、律师事务所工作经验优先。 专业技能：熟悉各类数据安全技术手段，了解各类技术手段的特点，能协助客户从法律、管理、技术等各层面完善跨境数据安全管理。熟悉《网络安全法》、《数据安全法》、《个人信息保护法》等法律法规，同时对境外包括GDPR等相关法律政策熟悉的优先。 工作能力：文字功底强，逻辑清晰，执行力强，能够独立撰写或组织撰写数据出境风险自评估报告；学习能力强，沟通能力佳，能够快速理解客户业务，并针对客户业务提出有效解决方案；具备一定的社交和谈判能力，能维护良好的客情关系；领导力强，善于领导团队合作，处理好团队内外部关系；有管理经验。 语言要求：英语能力强，能作为工作语言与客户交流。素质模型： 积极主动、团队合作意识强、诚实正直、真诚友善、敢于迎难而上、意志坚韧、自我管理意识强、双商高。

#### 公司介绍

一、关于数风科技 北京数风科技有限公司核心团队来自于国家互联网应急中心、网络空间安全协会等网络安全国家队。数风科技以“数据合规先行者”为使命，致力成为国内一流的跨境数据合规解决方案提供商，公司通过专业的技术和产品为客户提供更有效的数据合规解决方案，帮助客户提升网络数据风险管理和运营能力，现公司业务覆盖数据安全风险评估、数据风险检测、数据合规运营等多个领域。 二、关于数风科技数据出境风险自评估业务 2.1业务简介 我公司组建有专业数据安全评估团队，团队成员来自国家互联网应急中心、IBM、德恒等著名国家机构、咨询公司和律所，具备极强的政策理解、场景分析、风险管理、咨询整改能力，在数据合规和数据出境安全自评估等领域具备较强能力。 通过以数据出境风险自评服务，帮助数据处理者摸清存在出境行为的业务和数据基本情况，梳理出境数据的类型及敏感程度，以及可能对国家安全、公共利益、个人和组织合法权益带来的风险。为数据处理者数据出境风险管理工作提供必要基础和依据，便于数据处理者运用风险自评估结果，确保数据出境管理的要求和保障能力与评估所识别的风险相适应。如出境相关数据触发申报安全评估条件，协助数据处理者向国家网信部门申报数据出境安全评估，帮助数据处理者尽最大可能性申请到合规数据出境许可，促进数据处理者相关业务的发展。 此外，数据出境风险评估也将作为数据治理体系建设的起点和基础，就此打造一个完整的数据出境合规闭环，确保数据的高效利用和价值实现，通过改进决策、缩减成本、降低风险和提高安全合规等方式进一步回馈于业务。 2.2相关项目经验 数风科技2022年以来，专注数据出境合规领域，在江苏、浙江等多省参与办法试点相关工作。办法发布后，数风科技在北京、江苏、上海、浙江、广东等省份为大量头部互联网企业、头部外资企业提供数据出境风险自评估相关服务，涉足跨境电商、消费品、国际旅游、跨国车企、生物医药、国际物流、跨境清结算、跨境支付、AI识别等大量数据出境相关场景。 由数风科技提供数据出境风险自评估服务的江苏某互联网平台公司，成为江苏省首例，也是全国首家互联网企业、全国首家跨境电商、全国首家民营上市公司通过数据出境安全评估申报。此外数风科技提供相关服务的数据处理者中，有多家数据处理者的数据出境安全评估申报已经完成形式审核，被央办受理，正在安全评估环节。 2.3企业资质 2022年以来我公司深耕数据安全和数据合规领域，致力于提供规范、专业、标准化的服务，并取得了一些列相关企业资质。公司被CNCERT上海分中心评为网络安全应急服务支撑单位、中关村高新，同时获得了数据安全运营方向质量管理体系认证（ISO9001）、信息安全管理体系认证（ISO27001）、信息技术服务管理体系认证（ISO20000）等。

江苏康缘药业股份有限公司是集中药研发、生产、贸易为一体的大型中药企业， A股上市公司，被评为国家重点高新技术企业、国家创新型试点企业、国家技术创新示范企业、国家知识产权示范企业、中国制药工业百强企业（29位）。建有中药制药过程新技术国家重点实验室、中成药智能制造国家地方联合工程研究中心等国家级科研平台，是中国中药行业获新药证书最多、拥有发明专利最多的企业以及推进中药国际化最为深入的企业之一。康缘药业坚持体制创新和科技创新，建设了系统完善的江苏康缘现代中药研究院，拥有一支博硕士比例在70%以上的近500人的科研队伍。截至目前，上市了50余个现代中药新药，桂枝茯苓胶囊、热毒宁注射液、金振口服液、银杏二萜内酯葡胺注射液等创新中药产品已成为中医妇科、抗感染等治疗领域的知名品牌。承担“973”、“863”、国际合作、重大新药创制等国家科技计划50余项，拥有发明专利授权近500件，获得国家科技进步二等奖2项，国家技术发明二等奖1项，省部级科技进步一等奖8项，中国专利金奖2项，建成我国第一个中药智能生产工厂，是中药行业首个工信部批准的智能制造试点示范项目。已建设完成的中药智能化固体制剂工厂，项目达成后将全面实现从中药原料提取、精制到制剂的全过程自动化、信息化、智能化管控，具有极强的行业示范效应。放眼未来，公司将秉承“精品国药，康缘创造”的创新中药核心理念，大力发展现代中药，推进现代中药国际化，稳步发展大中药产业及生物制药业，为产业高质量发展以及保障人类健康作出更大贡献！

职位描述

1、负责项目区内安全管理队伍的建设与管理。2、熟悉治安、消防的有关法律知识。3、负责审核安全管理工作计划,制定岗位职责及考评办法。4、收集、整理安全管理工作的培训教材,组织安全主管制定培训计划并落实。5、定期主持召开安全管理工作会议。6、对部门质量合规运营负责，月度工作质量交付良好无扣款；7、对自有及第三方人员进行管理，保证人员稳定，负责人力屡约力交付；8、对部门资产及物耗进行管理，定期采购补充和盘点；9、负责部门品质运营，将品控问题控制在合理范围内；10、牵头组织检查各管理区域的治安、消防工作,协助地块内处理突发事件。11、对重大安全风险和消防重点部位或区域进行应急演练，对建筑物组织全员参与的消防演习演练，所有相关记录需存档。12、每季度安全消防预案演练不少于 1 次。消防重点单位消防演习每年不少于2 次。根据预案对项目出现的紧急事件***时间进行处理，含内部事件/事故/突发/异常事件/自然灾害等。13、例行和专项检查：例行组织安全消防例行检查，在季度末，节假日前，重大活动前，重点区域，接待活动前组织专项检查，检查结果或专项检查简报及时上报。14、动火作业：所有动火作业进行规范管理，对动火前，动火中，动火后进行监督管理，形成记录。15、风险评估：定期进行安全风险、消防风险评估并输出报告，并针对风险进行针对性方案完善并落地；16、有大型接待牵头经验并有处置安全及消防所遇所有突发事件的能历和经验；17、有良好的外联经验并配合行政对接属地各管辖单位。【岗位要求】1、大专及以上学历，年龄 35-45 岁；2、从事物业安全保卫管理岗位 7 年以上，熟悉安保部门各工作内容及流程，2年大型写字楼或园区类项目安全管理经验，团队管理 80 人以上，屡历较稳定。3、安全专业线条出身的物业项目经理或有 FM 管理经验/互联网职场从业经历者优先。4、熟悉安全消防相关法律法规，具备一定的组织管理能力和风险管理知识。5、具有专业的消防安全知识。以往工作中无重大安全事故。6、思维逻辑清晰，高潜力，具有极强的统筹管理能力、培训能力和现场管理能力。7、语言表达能力强，沟通能力强、责任心强，电脑使用熟练

职位介绍 岗位核心职责 1. 跨境数据安全体系搭建与落地：牵头构建覆盖国际化业务的数据安全管理体系，涵盖数据采集、传输、存储、处理、销毁全生命周期，制定统一的数据安全制度、流程规范及技术标准，确保体系适配不同国家/地区业务特性，实现全球数据安全管控标准化与本地化平衡。 2. 国际合规政策落地与风险管控：深度研读并落地GDPR、CCPA及拉美、亚太、非洲等目标市场数据安全与隐私保护法规，建立合规动态跟踪机制，及时同步政策更新并调整管控策略；主导数据合规风险评估、合规审查，防范跨境数据流转、本地化存储等场景的合规风险，保障业务合法合规运营。 3. 数据安全技术体系建设与优化：主导数据安全技术方案规划与落地，推动数据分类分级、脱敏、加密、访问控制、安全审计等技术工具的选型、部署与迭代，搭建数据安全监控与预警平台，实现数据安全风险的实时感知、快速响应与闭环处置。 4. 安全事件应急与治理：建立并完善国际化数据安全事件应急响应机制，制定应急预案并定期组织演练；牵头处置数据泄露、勒索、恶意爬取等安全事件，开展事件调查、根源分析、损失评估及整改复盘，降低事件影响范围与损失。 5. 跨部门协同与能力赋能：联动海外业务、法务、研发、运维、产品等团队，将数据安全要求融入业务全流程，解决业务发展中的安全痛点；开展数据安全培训与宣贯，提升全球团队数据安全意识与实操能力，推动数据安全文化落地。 6. 行业动态研判与策略迭代：跟踪全球数据安全技术趋势、行业实践及竞争对手安全策略，结合滴滴国际化业务发展阶段，优化数据安全体系与管控手段，提升整体安全防护能力，支撑业务全球化扩张。 任职资格要求 1. 工作经验：本科及以上学历，计算机、信息安全、法学等相关专业；8年以上数据安全、网络安全或跨境数据合规相关工作经验，有互联网、出行、本地生活服务行业经验者优先。 2. 专业能力：精通GDPR、CCPA等国际数据安全法规及主流海外市场合规要求，具备完整的公司级数据安全体系从0到1搭建与落地经验；熟悉数据全生命周期安全管控技术，掌握数据脱敏、加密、访问控制、安全审计等核心技术手段，能结合业务场景输出可落地的安全方案。 3. 风险管控与应急能力：具备敏锐的风险识别、评估与处置能力，有丰富的数据安全事件（泄露、勒索等）应急处置经验；熟悉安全风险评估、安全审计流程，能有效推动风险整改与闭环管理。 4. 协同与管理能力：具备出色的跨文化、跨部门沟通协调能力，能高效联动全球团队推动工作落地；拥有较强的项目管理能力与团队领导力，能带领团队应对复杂跨境安全场景挑战。 5. 职业素养：能熟练阅读英文法规文档、开展跨国沟通；具备强烈的责任心与主人翁意识，自驱上进、执行力强，能在快速变化的业务环境中平衡安全、合规与业务发展。 其他信息 语言要求：不限 行业要求：批发/零售,民航/铁路/公路/水路客运

赛思信安介绍

北京赛思信安技术股份有限公司成立于2007年，注册资金2100万，无外资背景。总部设立于北京，在南京设有全资子公司。公司拥有员工近200人，本科占62%、硕士占25%、博士占10%以上。其中，研发人员占80%以上。

赛思信安专注于公安、工信部、军队、安全等四大安全领域。多年来，公司依托扎实技术实力与丰富的实践经验，坚持走自主研发、培育自有品牌之路，获得了诸多软件著作权和发明专利，拥有多项注册商标，并在数据采集、数据存储、数据管理、数据安全、数据分析与服务等五个领域形成了丰富的产品线和特色的解决方案，可广泛满足安全领域用户对海量数据采集、存储、管理、保护及分析的多元化需求。

赛思信安通过了ISO9001质量管理体系认证和双软企业认证，并认定为“国家高新技术企业”和“中关村高新技术企业”，以及多项工信部及国家发改委项目资金支持。具有大数据相关产品著作权17项，发明专利24项，4款产品获得“北京市新技术新产品”证书。经过多年的沉淀，赛思信安已经快速成长为国内领先的大数据解决方案及服务提供商。

# Why Multinationals Are Suddenly Hiring China Cyber Compliance Experts | Dustin Kluttz 田馨纬 · LinkedIn · 2026-02-23

**Dustin Kluttz 田馨纬**: APAC Regional Security Officer at Atlas Copco Group with 8 years of experience. Previous roles include Cybersecurity & Compliance Lead China Operations at Atlas Copco Group, Cybersecurity Engineer IRS Cloud Migration Initiative at SHR Consulting Group, and Information System Security Officer (ISSO) at NOAA: National Oceanic & Atmospheric Administration. Based in Jing'an District, Shanghai, China [CN].

---

Why Multinationals Are Suddenly Hiring China Cyber Compliance Experts
Over the past 12–18 months, I’ve seen a clear shift.

Multinationals that once managed China data compliance from regional or global teams are now hiring dedicated, China-based cyber compliance talent.

This is not random.
It’s a response to enforcement reality.

China’s regulatory posture has matured. The laws are no longer “new.” Expectations are no longer theoretical. Audits are more structured. Fines are more visible. Regulators are more confident.And global teams are realizing something uncomfortable:

You cannot manage China cyber risk remotely.
Here’s why.

1️⃣ Enforcement is contextual.
China regulators interpret compliance through local practice, not just written law. Knowing the statute is not enough. You need to understand how it is applied on the ground.

2️⃣ Language and documentation matter.
Bilingual policies, localized procedures, regulator-facing materials. These are not cosmetic. They signal seriousness and preparation.

3️⃣ Cross-border analysis requires precision.
Standard contract thresholds. HR exemptions. Remote access exposure. Important data classification. These require someone who understands both global IT architecture and China regulatory nuance.

4️⃣ Regulator engagement is cultural.
How you respond during inquiry.
How you frame your controls.
How you demonstrate “rectification.”

These interactions are relationship-driven and context-sensitive.

Generic global compliance teams are excellent at ISO, NIST, GDPR, and enterprise governance.

But China’s CSL, DSL, PIPL, and MLPS ecosystem operates differently.

What I’m seeing now is proactive hiring.

CIOs and CISOs want someone in-country who can:
• Translate law into operational controls
• Interface directly with regulators
• Anticipate enforcement focus areas
• Align global architecture with China boundaries
• Prevent unnecessary filings or overexposure

This is not about headcount expansion.
It’s about risk containment. China represents revenue, manufacturing capacity, talent, and customer base.

When cyber compliance fails in China, the impact is not limited to a fine. It can affect operations, licensing, and business continuity.

If your China compliance strategy is still managed entirely offshore, it may be time to reassess. If you’re evaluating whether to build local capability or refine your current structure, contact me directly.

I can share what leading multinationals are doing differently and where enforcement pressure is actually increasing.
